summary: Fidel Castro suggested the Bienal, and the Ministry of Culture's Visual Arts Division organised the 1984 edition. Gerardo Mosquera writes the regime launched it with political aims, including promoting socialism and co-opting Third World intellectuals.
A royal decree in 1930 moved the Biennale from Venice's council to the fascist state, under president Giuseppe Volpi. Its archive history says it was seen as propping up a propaganda machine.
Bonaparte appointed Vivant Denon director of the Louvre in 1802, and Denon renamed it the Musée Napoléon. Denon displayed art seized in Napoleon's conquests as trophies of his victories.
King Louis-Philippe converted the palace into a Museum of the History of France, opened in 1837, to strengthen his legitimacy as king of all the French and reconcile supporters of earlier regimes.

n: Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts
summary: A government commission cleared 12 halls in 1949, put the museum's Western art in storage and filled them with gifts sent to Stalin for his 70th birthday. The display closed in 1953.

n: Sinchon Museum of American War Atrocities
summary: The museum presents North Korea's account that US troops killed over 35,000 people at Sinchon in 1950. Schools, army units and factories are sent on visits. Historian Adam Cathcart says the account underpinned anti-US propaganda.

Mansudae, founded in 1959, makes portraits, posters and monuments of the Kim leaders. Time reported in 2004 that North Korean state studios, Mansudae the best known, give artists salaried work on government commissions.
Founded 1953 and rebuilt 2013, when Kim Jong Un cut the ribbon. KCNA quoted Kim calling it a centre for anti-US and class education honouring Kim Il Sung's wartime victory over the United States.

State museum founded 1 August 1948 on Mansudae Hill to exhibit Kim Il Sung's revolutionary history. In April 2022 KCNA reported a new hall presenting Kim Jong Un's first decade, including his nuclear force declaration.
Opened October 1970 in the building where Kim Il Sung proclaimed the Workers' Party of Korea on 10 October 1945. Preserves the meeting hall and plays Kim's founding speech to visitors.
Opened to the public in 1970 beside Kim Il Sung's birthplace, a state designated revolutionary site. Exhibits present his childhood and portray his family members as patriot revolutionaries.
Founded by Kim Il Sung on 1 December 1945 and housed on Kim Il Sung Square since 1977. Exhibits run from the Stone Age to 1919 with political teaching on struggle against invaders and revolution.

Created on 12 December 1959 by a decree of the Ministry of the Revolutionary Armed Forces signed by Raúl Castro. Installed in the former Presidential Palace in 1974 to present the Revolution's history.

n: Belarusian State Museum of the History of the Great Patriotic War
summary: Founded 1944. The government built its new premises as its central politics of remembrance project, opened 2 July 2014 by Lukashenko and Putin. The exhibition keeps the Soviet heroic narrative of the war.

Syrian state war museum opened October 1999 under Hafez al-Assad, its panorama painted by North Korea's Mansudae Overseas Development Group. It presents the 1973 Quneitra assault as heroic victory and displays murals of Assad.
Conceived by Hosni Mubarak after a North Korea visit, built by North Korean artists and opened 5 October 1989. Run by the Egyptian military, it presents the 1973 war as unbroken victory.

Executive Order 14253 tasks Vice President Vance with removing improper ideology. The August 2025 White House letter ordered content corrections within 120 days. A July 2026 White House report accused it of ideological capture.

Named in the August 2025 White House letter ordering content corrections within 120 days under Executive Order 14253. In January 2026 the gallery removed Trump impeachment wall text after White House objections.

In January 2023 Russia's Culture Ministry asked the gallery to bring its displays into line with Putin's November 2022 decree on traditional spiritual and moral values. In February 2023 the ministry replaced director Zelfira Tregulova.

Ilham Aliyev commissioned the government-funded center, opened 2012 and named after his late father. Its Heydar Aliyev Museum presents the former president's life. An Oxford historian said it reinforces his personality cult.

North Korea converted Kim Il Sung's former office and residence into his mausoleum in 1995. Kim Jong Il's embalmed body joined his father's on display in December 2012. Visitors bow before both leaders.

Namibia's cabinet established the museum; North Korea's Mansudae Overseas Projects built it and President Pohamba opened it in March 2014. Scholars find it repeats the ruling SWAPO party's liberation narrative, conflating SWAPO with the nation.

Namibia's government commissioned the national memorial from North Korea's Mansudae Overseas Projects; it opened in August 2002. A 2017 Leiden study states the site legitimizes the rule of the former liberation movement SWAPO.

North Korean architects designed and built the national shrine from 1981 for Zimbabwe's new government. The ruling ZANU-PF Politburo confers national hero status and burial rights; critics in 2016 called it a partisan shrine.

President dos Santos's government commissioned the mausoleum; the MPLA and North Korea's government funded it and Mansudae Overseas Projects built it. Inaugurated in September 2012, it holds Neto's remains and hosts official state ceremonies.

Mussolini visited the Palazzo dell'Arte site in 1932; the building became a symbol of the Fascist party's building policy. The regime staged propaganda exhibitions there, and regime-aligned architects dominated the 1940 Triennale showcasing state projects.

In August 2025 the White House named the National Air and Space Museum among eight Smithsonian museums ordered to review content under Executive Order 14253. In January 2026 the Smithsonian handed over exhibition label photographs.

The state opened the Grand People's Study House in April 1982 for Kim Il Sung's 70th birthday as its national library and centre of Juche studies. Kim portraits hang throughout. Staff control access to materials.

Kim Il Sung founded the exhibition in 1946. It became the Three Revolutions Exhibition in 1983 and was enlarged in 1993. It presents industrial, agricultural and scientific achievements as successes of Juche ideology.
The hall opened in April 2002 to display flowers named after Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il. Festivals on the leaders' birthdays show arrangements from state bodies beside rocket and satellite models.

The palace opened in 1989 under the Korean Youth Corps. Children perform regularly for tourists, singing and dancing in praise of the nation's achievements. KCNA reports the performances as pledges of loyalty to the leaders.

Abdoulaye Wade commissioned the monument, built by North Korea's Mansudae Overseas Projects and inaugurated on 3 April 2010. Wade claimed 35 percent of tourist revenue as intellectual property. Critics called it a presidential vanity project.

Hitler had the building erected and opened it on 18 July 1937 for the annual Great German Art Exhibitions, held to 1944. His photographer Heinrich Hoffmann took charge of selecting works, and Hitler decided finally.

The SED Politburo decided in 1950 to found the GDR's central history museum, and the Central Committee approved its staff. It presented a Marxist-Leninist view of history that legitimised the GDR until 1990.
Created in 1935 and opened in 1936, the Central Lenin Museum housed the Lenin cult under the Communist Party. Its first exhibit showed Stalin close to Lenin, and Stalin was cut after 1956.

n: State Museum of the History of Religion
summary: The USSR Ministry of Culture took over the museum in 1961. Its directors from 1968 to 1987, trained at the Party's atheism institute, built an atheist propaganda programme of lectures and touring exhibitions.

A foundation funded mainly by Gazprom, with the presidential administration as partner, runs the parks. Historian Ivan Kurilla calls them an ideological tool, and Bumaga reported pro-war exhibits in 2023.
President Ilham Aliyev proposed and opened the park, and his website says it shows the victory and Armenian war crimes. Until October 2021 it displayed wax figures of Armenian soldiers.

n: Museum of the Communist Party of China
summary: The Party Central Committee decided in 2017 to build it. People's Daily, the Party paper, reports the Central Propaganda Department led construction. Xi Jinping called it a spiritual home for Party members, China Daily reports.

Reviewing Denton's study, Joseph Allen says official ideology has driven Chinese museums since 1949. Time found the 2011 Road to Rejuvenation display sanitized and pro-government. Xi Jinping gave his Chinese Dream speech there in 2012.

The Nanjing municipal government built it in 1985. Emily Matson (Wilson Center) finds its phases track the Communist Party's changing legitimizing narrative. Contested Histories reports state-defined aims, including patriotic education.

n: Museum of the War of Chinese People's Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
summary: Mitter (China Quarterly, 2000) says Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Qiaomu authorized it and that it shapes official memory legitimizing Party rule. A patriotic education base for Hong Kong youth opened there in 2025.

Opened in 1959 as an exhibit of the landlord's crimes. Ho and Li report officials fabricated evidence such as a water dungeon, and denounced class enemies faced show trials there in the Cultural Revolution.

Vietnamese authorities appointed Mai Lam to turn S-21 into a museum in 1979. Rachel Hughes finds the Kampuchean Ministry of Culture, Information and Propaganda oversaw it and used foreign visits to support the regime's legitimacy.

n: National Museum of the Islamic Revolution and Holy Defense
summary: The Tehran municipality built it. Its statute was amended in 2021 with Supreme Leader Khamenei's approval and published by the Armed Forces General Staff. AFP reported that it glorifies the Iran-Iraq war.

n: Victory Museum (Central Museum of the Great Patriotic War)
summary: Since April 2022 the federal museum has staged exhibitions such as Ordinary Nazism and Ordinary NATOzism presenting Ukraine's army as heirs of wartime Nazi collaborators, echoing the Kremlin's denazification justification for the invasion.

The Defence Ministry created the park in 2015 for military-patriotic education of youth; in August 2023 it displayed Western armoured vehicles captured in Ukraine during the Army-2023 forum, inspected by Dmitry Medvedev.

The first Orbán government opened it on 24 February 2002 under Orbán's adviser Mária Schmidt; historians criticised its equation of fascism and communism and its casting of Hungary as a victim of foreign occupiers.

n: Museum of the Second World War
summary: In April 2017 the PiS government merged the museum, dismissed director Paweł Machcewicz and installed Karol Nawrocki, who altered the exhibition; from June 2024 the new management reversed those changes, restoring the authors' original vision.

Opened by the new communist authorities on 4 September 1975 as the Exhibition House for US and Puppet Crimes, renamed in 1990 and 1995; anthropologist Christina Schwenkel describes its uncontextualised self-representation of American war crimes.

Created by Communist Party resolutions of 1970 and 1977 and opened in 1990, the state museum is tasked by ministerial decision with propaganda and education on Ho Chi Minh's thought and revolutionary ideals.

The AKP-run Istanbul municipality's Kültür A.Ş. opened it in 2009 to convey the spirit of the 1453 conquest; Posocco (2018) analyses it as a case of AKP-era museums promoting Ottoman and Islamic nationalism.

Established in 1882 under the Imperial Army and made a state institution of the Army Ministry by imperial decree in 1910, it ran national spiritual mobilisation exhibitions in the 1930s until September 1945.

The National Fascist Party under Dino Alfieri staged the Mostra della Rivoluzione Fascista here from 28 October 1932, opened by Mussolini, behind a fasces facade by Libera and De Renzi; nearly four million people attended.
Built 1976 to 1980 to commemorate Chiang Kai-shek with a giant statue and military honour guard; the Ministry of Culture began a transitional justice project in 2017 and removed the guard in 2024.

After Chávez died in March 2013 the Maduro government turned the barracks of his 1992 coup into his mausoleum and museum, with honour guard, daily cannon salute and state-staged narrative placing him beside Bolívar.

n: National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War
summary: Opened in 1981 by Leonid Brezhnev as the Ukrainian State Museum of the History of the Great Patriotic War, beneath a Motherland statue bearing the Soviet emblem, to commemorate the Soviet war narrative.

From 1933 the museum served Nazi racial ideology as a propaganda machine of racial hygiene, co-producing with NSDAP offices the touring exhibitions Blut und Rasse (1935 to 1938) and Ewiges Volk (1937 to 1939).

n: Museum of Contemporary History of Russia
summary: In April 2022 the museum opened NATO, Chronicle of Cruelty with Defense Ministry trophies from Ukraine; in 2024 it co-wrote the Culture Ministry's guidelines for special military operation exhibitions nationwide.

Soviet authorities opened the museum complex in 1957, a year after Khrushchev's secret speech, as a monument honouring Stalin; a 2012 Georgian plan to refocus it on his atrocities was never carried out.
The City of Belgrade built the museum in 1962 as a 70th birthday gift to Tito, to display and preserve the gifts he received; after his death in 1980 it became the Tito Memorial Centre.

Hoxha's regime built the museum from 1978 and opened it in 1981 with displays shaped to the communist narrative and a socialist realist mosaic; after 1991 the red star and worker's red book were removed.
Suharto's Army History Centre opened the museum in 1992; its 34 dioramas present the New Order account of PKI treachery in 1965 and omit the mass killings that followed.

Hun Sen's government built the memorial, opened 2018, to honour his win-win policy; carvings depict his political triumphs including the 2017 dissolution of the opposition CNRP, and the museum shows his achievements.
The Party and state built the hall in 1976 to 1977 to display Mao's embalmed body; the Party designates it a national patriotic education demonstration base.

n: Hong Kong Museum of the War of Resistance and Coastal Defence
summary: The 2023 Policy Address ordered the Museum of Coastal Defence converted to strengthen national pride and patriotism; the government renamed it on 3 September 2024 as a patriotic education base.

Franco's Ministry of Education created the museum by decree in 1941 within the Hispanidad ideology; its decree said it should inspire Spaniards and its displays presented conquest and colonisation as a civilising, evangelising project.

Under Cipriano Efisio Oppo the 1931 to 1943 Quadriennali built consensus for the fascist regime; the 1935 halls celebrated regime policies and Mussolini, and the 1939 edition ran under ministerial supervision and racial laws.

After 1948 the Communist Party made the memorial its pantheon; the Central Committee opened the Klement Gottwald Mausoleum there in December 1953, run by an Interior Ministry department until the body was cremated in 1962.

The Estado Novo's SNI opened the museum in July 1948 from the 1940 exhibition's Centro Regional; the SNI managed it directly and its rural ethnographic vision of national identity served António Ferro's política do espírito.

n: Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution
summary: The Central Military Commission approved the PLA museum in 1959 and it opened in 1960 under the General Political Department. The Central Publicity Department named it a national patriotic education base in 1997.

n: Memorial of the Site of the First National Congress of the CPC
summary: The Shanghai Party committee bought the Party's birthplace in 1952 and opened it as a memorial, named a national patriotic education base in 1997; a tripled memorial hall opened for the 2021 centenary.

The state founded the hall in 1950 to display the Party's Yan'an years and listed the Yan'an sites as national patriotic education bases in 1997; Xi took the Politburo Standing Committee there in 2022.

n: Memorial Hall of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
summary: Built by the state in 1958 as China's only Korean War museum and listed as a national patriotic education base in 1997. Expanded on central approval, it reopened in 2020 for the war's 70th anniversary.

n: Museo de la Revolución Democrática y Cultural
summary: Evo Morales's government opened the state-built museum in his birthplace in 2017 to show his life, the gifts he received and his achievements. Critics called it a personality cult; it closed after his 2019 fall.
The Party Politburo decided in 1992 to build a museum to the Party's founder; Vietnam funded it and it opened in 2000. The Party's Propaganda and Training Board holds its anniversary exhibitions.

Sheikh Hasina's trust opened the museum in her father's house in 1994; as prime minister she held state salutes and party ceremonies there each August. Protesters burned it in 2024 and razed it in 2025.

President Chadli unveiled the Maqam Echahid complex in 1982 to represent national unity and strengthen the FLN regime's legitimacy, Sarah Gray writes in Ibraaz. The museum has run under the Ministry of Mujahideen since 1993.

The army's General Political Department built the new museum, opened in 2024 to honour the People's Army and its defence tradition. Party chief To Lam called it a red address for studying the Party's leadership.

The Ministry of Culture opened the museum in 2012 inside the Presidential Administration to present the presidential state since 1994, with Lukashenko's first decrees and gifts to him; he called its opening politically important.

King Leopold II created the museum in 1898 from the 1897 Brussels exposition's colonial section as a propaganda tool for his Congo colonial project; the 1910 building was opened to showcase the Belgian Congo.

n: Palais de la Porte Dorée (Musée national de l'histoire de l'immigration)
summary: Built 1928 to 1931 as the Musée des Colonies for the Paris Colonial Exhibition, the palace was a propaganda work made to promote the benefits of colonisation and the merits of the French empire.

The Colonial Institute's statutes charged its museum, opened 1926 with Ministry of Colonies funding, with promoting all interests stemming from the colonial possessions, an aim described as colonial propaganda; renamed in 1950.

The Estado Novo rebuilt the 1940 Portuguese World Exhibition monument in concrete in 1960 for the Henry the Navigator quincentenary; scholars call it the regime's brand image and a monument of its ideology.
Inaugurated 16 December 1949 by Prime Minister Malan with mostly government funding, the monument gave the new National Party government a stage to celebrate the volk and articulate white supremacy.
Opened by the KMT government in 1965, the museum served to assert the KMT's legitimacy as the sole legitimate Chinese government and to educate Taiwanese about their Chinese heritage.

Run by the Turkish General Staff since 1980, Anıtkabir presents an authorized version of Turkish history; official visits and ceremonies honour Atatürk and the Republic, re-sacralising the Atatürk cult.
